coverage.evidence: HelixChatProvider.cs:411-414 and 436-439 pick the sender in this order: CustomBotSenderAsync, then SharedBotSenderAsync, then OwnerSenderAsync (own bot, then shared bot, then the streamer's own account). The page table, rows 1 to 3, matches.

IChannelTwitchBotResolver.cs:16-19 and ChannelTwitchBotResolver.cs:30-55 return the channel's own active bot first, else the connected shared bot. BotNotModeratorSource.cs reads that bot. ChatPlatformRouter.cs:545-567 HasDedicatedBotAsync drops the marker. Page lines 22 and 74 match.

ChatPlatformRouter.cs:57-60 (self-host default: types as the streamer's own account). HelixChatProvider.cs OwnerSenderAsync is the last fallback. TwitchTokenResolver.cs:80-81 falls back to the owner connection. Page lines 6-8 and row 3 match.

ChannelService.cs:561-570 ValidateBotLinePrefix: empty is valid, more than 4 UTF-16 units or any whitespace is refused. ApplyAndPersist stores null for an empty string. BasicsView.vue:279 sets maxlength 4. Page step 2, the emoji note (UTF-16 Length) and line 63 match.

ChatPlatformRouter.cs:521-537 applies the prefix only when HasDedicatedBotAsync is false. Lines 545-567 count either an active channel bot authorization or a connected shared bot. Lines 247-249 never prefix an asBroadcaster send. Page lines 46-48 and 70 match.

dashboard/src/views/dashboard/settings/i18n/en.json:88-91 has the title 'Bot line marker' and the description 'Shown before lines the bot posts through your own account.' BasicsView.vue:272-283 renders it on Bot basics. Page line 45 matches.

dashboard/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1170-1171 (the card cites 1163-1164, which has drifted) holds the title '{botName} is not a moderator in your channel' and the message 'Type /mod {botName} in your Twitch chat. Twitch limits what a bot without the moderator role can do.' BotNotModeratorSource.cs sets botName to bot.Username. BotModeratorRoleChangeHandler.cs clears the notice on channel.moderator.add. Page lines 77-85 match.

reader_answers.evidence: Owner fallback: HelixChatProvider.cs OwnerSenderAsync, last in the chain at 436-439. Order: HelixChatProvider.cs:411-414.

Twitch must be connected first for OwnerSenderAsync to find a connection. PUT settings/basics needs setup:write (ChannelsController.cs:599-600), which is seeded at Broadcaster level and cannot be granted (ActionDefinitionSeeder.cs:437). The shared bot is added in setup (site/setup/i18n/en.json:19, 33) or on the admin Platform bot page (admin/i18n/en.json:842-850).

WhiteLabelBotView.vue:47-70 and 116-120 set the row name: the bot name with a Connected state and an @login, or shared.titleNamed with the login, or shared.title. Texts: white-label-bot/i18n/en.json:5, 8, 14-15. AuthService.cs:1400-1456 returns a login only for a connected own bot or shared bot. 'Basics saved.' is in settings/i18n/en.json:80 (BasicsView.vue:236). !commands goes through SendReplyViaAsync, which adds the prefix (ChatPlatformRouter.cs:298-305). Broadcasters skip the cooldown (ChatMessageHandler.cs:1949-1950).

With a dedicated bot connected, HasDedicatedBotAsync is true and the prefix is null (ChatPlatformRouter.cs:532-536). BotNotModeratorSource.cs raises the item for the resolver's bot. The NeedsAttentionPanel.vue and ErrorInbox.vue lists both read useActionRequired. The 'Action required' title is in en.json:1031. The item clears through BotModeratorRoleChangeHandler.cs on channel.moderator.add.
